title: layer satisfaction subtracts nominal capability rows and nothing else: a capability an author spells `TypeScript` cannot buy a native pin over `eval`

xfail.reason: The fork accepts this program, grants the pin, and RUNS it. Measured 2026-08-23 through conformance/runner/backend-go.mjs: zero diagnostics, exit 0, stdout ["1"] — where the reference reports SMITHERS3001@21:1. This is a SUBTRACTION defect and not a missing walk, and the two probes that separate them were run: (1) the same program with the capability class renamed `Config` and everything else byte-identical is REFUSED by the fork, `native pin failed: TypeScript is required through main.sm#scoped -> main.sm#<anonymous>`, so the fork does enter the provide callback and does classify `eval` as `TypeScript`; (2) a `Layer.provide` whose callback reads `process.pid` is refused there too. The ONLY thing that changes between the refused program and this one is the identifier on the capability class. So the fork's layer satisfaction subtracts by matching the row NAME and has no guard for the built-in requirements a native pin exists to reject, and `abstract class TypeScript extends Context` is one identifier away from certifying `eval` as native-portable. The reference has the guard explicitly: poc/src/targets/classify.ts's `charge` refuses to drop any requirement `blocksNativePin` recognizes (`TypeScript`, `Module<...>`, `Host<...>`). This is the highest-severity shape a fail-open can take in this area, because the exploiting program looks ordinary, compiles clean, and runs.
xfail.doc: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Satisfaction' (Locked): 'Providing a layer to a computation MUST remove matching capabilities from the computation's unsatisfied requirement row.' The word that carries it is CAPABILITIES — the nominal context rows a layer produces. specification/requirements.mdx, 'TypeScript Requirement' (Locked), introduces `TypeScript` as a BUILT-IN capability 'representing runtime dependence on TypeScript/JavaScript-specific behavior', which is a fact about the compiled program and not a service any `Layer.succeed` supplies. specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native Pin' (Locked): 'Compilation MUST fail if any reachable operation or provider requires TypeScript' — the sentence names PROVIDERS explicitly and makes them a reason to fail, never a way to be satisfied.

notes: The hostile input is the reason this is a case rather than a comment: a capability's row name is a class name, class names are whatever the author writes, and `abstract class TypeScript extends Context` is legal Smithers, so a subtraction implemented as a name match over the requirement row is one identifier away from certifying `eval` as native-portable. This case is the guard on the subtraction that 21-native-pin/a-layer-provided-capability-is-subtracted-and-the-pin-still-holds requires to exist, and the two must be read together: the safe way to satisfy this one alone is to subtract nothing, and the safe way to satisfy that one alone is to subtract everything. `messageContains` pins the requirement name and the route together, so a diagnostic that fired for some other reason cannot satisfy it. `eval` is the same `TypeScript` contributor 18-typescript-requirement and 21-native-pin/a-pin-reaching-typescript-is-rejected pin independently, so this case measures the interaction and not the classification.
